transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-11-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood DevRel), Maya (BlueArc ML), Ravi (BlueArc Platform), Ellen (BlueArc Product), Tom (BlueArc intern)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, rough):
- Walkthrough of Redwood SDK quickstart for Python and TS, environment variable and secrets setup, CI/CD example (GitHub Actions).
- Console tour focusing on routes, keys, and Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization).
- Compliance questions: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployment options.
- Next steps: quickstart repo, micro-benchmark, security packet, pilot scheduling.

Topics covered:
- local auth + API key best practices
- secrets in CI (GH Actions) and vault integrations
- Redwood Console: routes, models, traces
- Redwood Optimize recommendations and when to apply quantization
- Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:10] Maya: Hey I'm Maya, lead ML, we own the recommendation infra at BlueArc.
[00:15] Ravi: Ravi, platform eng, I'll own deployment and CI.
[00:20] Ellen: Ellen, product. Tom - intern is with us too.
[00:28] Alex: Great. Samir I'll hand-off to you for the live dev walkthrough but i'll cover the console bits later. Jules will chime in on quickstarts.
[00:35] Samir: Cool. so goal today is pair-programming style: get you running the minimal quickstart in Python, show TS equivalent, show env var and secrets flow, then demo the Console Optimize panel. we'll poke at latency/cost tradeoffs.
[00:52] Tom: Quick note, we're running an internal service on kubernetes, and we have strict secrets policy - we use Hashi and a company vault.
[01:00] Samir: great that's common. quick note: for local dev we still recommend a short-lived API key rather than embedding long lived keys in code. i'll show how to wire up a vault-to-GHA step.
[01:18] Samir: ok i'm sharing my screen. first file: quickstart/python/README.md - here's the snippet:
[01:26] Samir (reading): "export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx" then pip install redwood-client then from redwood import RedwoodClient; c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) response = c.generate('Summarize this order...')"
[01:45] Maya: are those real package names? i saw earlier the pypi package is called red-infer?
[01:52] Samir: ah yeah sorry the published name in our org is "redwood-infer"—the auto transcript sometimes collapses names. we'll include exact pip/npm names in the repo i send.
[02:08] [Minor crosstalk]
[02:15] Samir: moving onto TS quickstart: npm install @redwood/inference; then const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ messages: [...] })
[02:31] Ravi: for server side node we'll put env in k8s secrets and mount as env var. for CI we want to avoid printing keys in logs. any recommendations for GitHub Actions?
[02:44] Jules: we have a short GH Actions snippet in the quickstart: uses actions/setup-node then uses the repo secret REDWOOD_API_KEY and injects into env. example step: uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials (for deploy) then run: echo ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }} | some-tool. But more recommended is to have the CI fetch short-lived tokens from your vault at build time.
[03:09] Maya: does Redwood support short-lived tokens or role-based tokens? I mean, we can't share a single key across teams.
[03:18] Alex: Redwood supports API keys plus AWS STS + mTLS in private deploys. for Hosted we have per-token TTLs and you can rotate keys via the Console. Dedicated customers can use our private KMS integration for envelope encryption.
[03:34] Samir: and RBAC is available in the Console so you can create a key scoped to only embeddings or only generate routes. we'll show the Console policy for that in a sec.
[03:48] [04:00] Samir: let's actually switch to Console. i'm navigating to console.redwood.ai (note: in transcription this sometimes shows as redwood-console). here is the "Routes" page - each route maps to an API key/ingress config and you can pin a model version.
[04:20] Samir: route example: "recommendation-infer" pinned to 1.4-quant. you can set batch size and latency SLO. when you change a route you can do canary rollout.
[04:35] Maya: pinned to 1.4-quant, is that safe for production? we worry about quality regressions with quantized models.
[04:43] Samir: good question. Optimize can run evals against your prompt set to show quality delta. we usually recommend running the evals workspace first: pick critical prompts (10-50) and compare topk metrics. if degradation is low you can use quantized to save cost.
[04:58] Ellen: what's the monitoring story on hallucination/regressions?
[05:05] Jules: Console has a Quality dashboard that ties to an eval set; you can set regression alerts, and there's a drift trace that shows token-level probs for suspect completions.
[05:20] Ravi: for throughput, we expect bursty traffic around sales events; can Dedicated autoscale?
[05:26] Samir: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity into our shared pool. Private on-prem or VPC has autoscaling too but depends on your infra provisioning. capacity planning is something we help with in onboarding.
[05:44] [06:00] Maya: compliance: SOC2 is a blocker; we also need audit logs and KMS integration.
[06:07] Alex: Redwood's SOC2 report and security whitepaper are in the security packet i'll send. we support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated via AWS KMS/HSM. audit logs and request traces are available in Console with long-term retention as an add-on.
[06:28] Maya: ok please send that.
[06:32] Samir: quick pause, back to the quickstart. i'll do a live run of the python example with a small request so you see end-to-end.
[06:40] [Screen shows terminal]
[06:45] Samir: pip install redwood-infer==0.12.3 ; export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... ; python quickstart/example.py
[06:55] Samir (typing): running now... response took 230ms, tokens: input 12, output 48.
[07:05] Tom: 230ms? that's great. is that on hosted or dedicated?
[07:10] Samir: Hosted in us-west. latency depends on model and seq length. we also optionally warm KV cache for conversational apps.
[07:20] Maya: how do we do prefix caching? we have a per-user context size we want to cache to reduce repeated compute.
[07:27] Samir: we expose KV cache management via the SDK and Console. you can prefill the cache for active sessions and we persist against route-level caches. it's in the SDK as client.cache.prefill(session_id, token_buffer). we'll add that to the repo.
[07:46] [08:00] Samir: now switching to TypeScript quickstart. i'll open quickstart/ts/examples/chat.ts and run node. code shows client.chat.create with streaming support. Jules, anything to add on streaming?
[08:15] Jules: streaming is enabled by default in the SDK; we provide SSE and WebSocket client helpers. if you're running in serverless, use the chunked-response handler. we've seen customers mis-handle backpressure so we'll share a sample middleware.
[08:31] Ravi: any recommended max batch size for our traffic pattern? we do sub-100ms p95 target.
[08:38] Samir: with p95 <100ms you want batch sizes minimal, maybe 1-4 depending on model. Optimize will recommend batching config based on your observed qps/latency. the Console Optimize panel shows tradeoffs: cost per token vs median latency.
[08:54] Maya: can Optimize push config changes automatically or is it advisory?
[08:58] Alex: it's advisory by default. there is an opt-in autopilot for batch sizing but most customers prefer manual rollouts. we support canary/incremental apply.
[09:12] [09:30] Samir: ok now for CI: here's a GH Actions example in .github/workflows/deploy.yml Step: - name: Fetch secrets from Vault - uses: hashicorp/vault-action@v2 - with: url, token; then - name: Set REDWOOD_API_KEY - run: echo "REDWOOD_API_KEY=${{ steps.vault.outputs.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV. careful not to echo keys in logs.
[09:55] Ravi: that pattern looks workable. we will integrate via our vault sidecar that injects secrets at runtime.
[10:02] Samir: great. next, quick note on network configuration for Private: you can deploy Redwood Private inside your VPC and use private endpoints; we support mTLS and customer peering. there's also an air-gapped deployment option for sensitive workloads.
[10:22] Maya: for data residency we need eu-west storage for any logs, is that supported?
[10:28] Alex: yes, region-level retention and residency controls are part of the Private offering and also available in Dedicated via region pinning.
[10:36] [10:50] Ellen: on cost, can you show a sample bill for a typical recommendation workload?
[10:55] Samir: i don't have a detailed invoice on screen, but our cost model is token-based plus optional per-minute reserved capacity for Dedicated. I'll send a sample workbook. we can model your traffic with the benchmark results.
[11:12] Maya: what's the onboarding timeline if we want to pilot next month?
[11:16] Alex: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: quickstart + small traffic pilot, then micro-benchmarks and model/quantization recommendation. Dedicated provisioning adds lead time but a hosted pilot can start same week.
[11:30] Samir: ok let's do the micro-benchmark approach now: can you share a small sample of production prompts we can run? 100-500 examples are ideal.
[11:38] Maya: yes we'll prepare 200 prompts.
[11:40] Samir: perfect. we'll run them with hosted and quantized variants and share the metrics.
[11:47] [12:00] Samir: quick demo of Optimize panel: here the Optimize tab shows suggested batch sizes, suggested quantization profile (int8-channel vs float16) and an estimated cost save. remember these are heuristics until you run evals.
[12:20] Maya: can you annotate recommendations with expected quality deltas?
[12:24] Jules: yes Optimize runs an eval and reports quality delta, you can set a tolerance threshold. we'll show that in the repo's evals/README.
[12:36] Ravi: for our infra, we need a terraform module for route creation and key rotation, do you have an infra-as-code example?
[12:45] Samir: we have a terraform provider snippet: resource "redwood_route" "recommend" { name = "rec" model = "redwood/rec-1" max_tokens = 256 } we'll include it, but note provider is beta for some features.
[12:59] Maya: concerning rate-limits, if we hit throttling in hosted what happens to in-flight requests?
[13:05] Alex: we return 429s with retry-after; we also recommend client-side exponential backoff and server-side queueing. Dedicated has a higher throughput SLA to avoid throttles.
[13:17] Tom: small question, for streaming in TS can we pipe chunks through our existing SSE consumer?
[13:23] Jules: yes, the SDK emits chunk events compatible with standard EventSource handlers. we'll paste a sample middleware.
[13:35] [14:00] Maya: ok i'm trying to think of final blockers: SOC2 docs, KMS integration, pilot start date, and micro-benchmark.
[14:09] Alex: action items we'll recap: i'll share the quickstart repo and security packet; Samir will run micro-bench and share metrics; Maya will send sample prompts and compliance contact.
[14:24] Ellen: timeline: we can target pilot kickoff Nov 27 if paperwork is ok.
[14:29] Alex: sounds good. anything else?
[14:33] Ravi: one last technical deep dive - after the pilot we may request a latency deep-dive with your infra team.
[14:38] Samir: happy to do that.
[14:42] Alex: ok thanks everyone. i'll follow up with the repo, console screenshots, and SOC2 packet.
[14:50] Maya: thanks all.

End of meeting.
